summary: Two files changed, no production code. The OpenCode Envoy plugin's Dispatch-tools test now reads its expected tool names from the shared contract's dispatchToolSpecs and keeps one explicit required-argument expectation per tool as a map keyed by tool name (five lists corrected to what the contract requires today, the two new tools added with empty lists); the ask-execution assertions are unchanged. The envoy-plugin CI job gained a `Test envoy plugin` step between Typecheck and Pack, and that step ran green on the pull request's own run. PR #1086, head 8c7a1d1f1ee14519d9039bc1186c4cd218bc4edd.

proof.criterion: 1. `bun test packages/envoy-plugin/src/__tests__/dispatch-tools.test.ts` passes from the repository root with no Dispatch variables in the environment.
proof.surface: Bun test runner from the root of the issue workspace (the exact command the spec names), with the pane's DISPATCH_URL/DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE/DISPATCH_TOKEN scrubbed for the command. For a test-and-CI-only change this local run plus the spec's negative controls is the production-like surface; the CI step itself is proven on the pull request (proof 3).
proof.command: cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && env -u DISPATCH_URL -u DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE -u DISPATCH_TOKEN bun test packages/envoy-plugin/src/__tests__/dispatch-tools.test.ts
proof.observed: `1 pass, 0 fail, 32 expect() calls, Ran 1 test across 1 file`, exit 0. Pre-fix at parent 7ef4ffae (plan handoff on main a197cdc0) the same command exits 1 with `- Expected - 0 / + Received + 2` naming dispatch_request_approval and dispatch_open_asks. Whole plugin suite (`bun run test` in packages/envoy-plugin, same scrub): `61 pass, 0 fail, 137 expect() calls, Ran 61 tests across 7 files`, exit 0; `bun run lint`: `Checked 14 files in 109ms. No fixes applied.` exit 0; `bun run typecheck`: exit 0.
proof.negativeControl: Throwaway `if (spec.name === "dispatch_search") continue;` inserted as the first line inside `for (const spec of dispatchToolSpecs) {` in packages/envoy-plugin/src/server.ts → the same command exits 1: `expect(received).toEqual(expected)` with `-   "dispatch_search",` under `- Expected - 1 / + Received + 0`, at dispatch-tools.test.ts:74. Reverted with `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" restore packages/envoy-plugin/src/server.ts`; `jj diff --stat` afterwards lists only the workflow, the test file, and the provisioned .omp/config.yml.

proof.criterion: 2. The test derives its expected tool list from the shared contract (dispatchToolSpecs) rather than a hand-typed list.
proof.surface: The test file itself (source check) plus the same root Bun runner for the negative half.
proof.observed: Exit 0 with exactly two hits: line 2 `import { dispatchIssueSubject, dispatchToolSpecs } from "@legion/contracts";` and line 75 `dispatchToolSpecs.map((spec) => spec.name)`; no `expectedDispatchTools` remains. Tool names are spelled out only as keys of the `requiredArguments` map (typed `Record<string, readonly string[]>`, not an exhaustive key type), which the spec keeps by design.
proof.negativeControl: Throwaway change of the names assertion's expected value to `[...dispatchToolSpecs.map((spec) => spec.name), "dispatch_bogus"]` → `env -u DISPATCH_URL -u DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE -u DISPATCH_TOKEN bun test packages/envoy-plugin/src/__tests__/dispatch-tools.test.ts` exits 1 with `-   "dispatch_bogus",` under `- Expected - 1 / + Received + 0`. Reverted by hand to `dispatchToolSpecs.map((spec) => spec.name)` (never `jj restore`, the test file is the change); the positive command re-run: `1 pass, 0 fail, 32 expect() calls`.

proof.criterion: 3. On this issue's pull request, the `envoy-plugin` job of the "Legion Envoy and Contracts" workflow shows a `Test envoy plugin` step that runs `bun run test` in packages/envoy-plugin, and that step is green.
proof.surface: GitHub Actions on pull request #1086 itself, read through `legion gh` (run 34823844127, job 103911344323).
proof.command: legion gh -- run view 34823844127 --repo sjawhar/legion --json jobs --jq '.jobs[] | select(.name=="envoy-plugin") | {conclusion, steps: [.steps[] | {name, conclusion}]}' ; legion gh -- run view 34823844127 --repo sjawhar/legion --log --job 103911344323
proof.observed: Job conclusion `success`; steps in order: Lint envoy plugin (success), Typecheck envoy plugin (success), Test envoy plugin (success), Pack envoy plugin (success). The step's log shows `$ bun test`, `bun test v1.4.2`, `61 pass`, `0 fail`, `Ran 61 tests across 7 files. [1.97s]`. Run headSha 8c7a1d1f1ee14519d9039bc1186c4cd218bc4edd, event pull_request, conclusion success. `legion gh -- pr checks 1086`: envoy-plugin pass, changes pass; the `Tests` workflow run 34823844078 (lint, typecheck, test) and `PR Title` run 34823844203 all pass at the same head; the other six path-filtered jobs skipped as expected.
proof.negativeControl: Per the plan, no red head was pushed to watch the step fail (a CI slot on a queue Sami has said is too long and slow, 2026-09-11). The evidence that the step gates is the pre-fix run of the same script this step executes: at parent 7ef4ffae (main a197cdc0), `bun run test` in packages/envoy-plugin exits 1 with 60 pass / 1 fail on this very test — that is what the step would have reported on any plugin PR before this change.

trickyParts: `legion gh -- pr create` run from inside the issue workspace fails with `fatal: not a git repository: /home/ubuntu/.local/state/legion/.../.git/worktrees/legion-96` — the colocated worktree's .git pointer names a path from the box the clone was made on. With --repo, --base, and --head all explicit the command needs no local repository, so it was run from /tmp. `gh run`/`gh pr checks` reads were run the same way.

The provisioned working copy (.omp/config.yml, no description) sits above the implementation commit, so `jj bookmark set legion/LEGION-96` defaulting to @ would point the bookmark at an unpushable commit; the bookmark was moved to @- with --allow-backwards (the workspace was provisioned with the bookmark on the fresh working copy) and pushed from there.
deviations: None from the plan. The five corrected required-argument lists the planner discovered (dispatch_ask, dispatch_comment, dispatch_suggest, dispatch_doc_edit, dispatch_artifact) are in the map exactly as the spec's Requirements table (version 3) now states.
